current.text: He is expected to be available on opening night after ankle surgery. Reports say he is fully ready for the start of the season.
He will probably not play in preseason, and some days off are expected during the season.
Experts still see a high risk that he gets hurt again.
He is projected to start at center for Memphis.
Expect about 25 to 28 minutes a night, not 30 or more. Memphis wants to manage his large frame. Isaiah Stewart and Quinten Post will take the extra center minutes.
Coach Tuomas Iisalo keeps minutes down and runs an 11 or 12 man rotation. That also caps Edey's minutes.
One expert projects about 65 games, partly because Edey is thinking about his contract extension.
Take him in the 60s or 70s. Experts call him a top 60 player at worst and see a top 50 per game finish as reasonable. Lloyd calls him a possible league winner.
If he played 30 minutes a night, he would be a top 30 player.
At his ESPN rank of about 113 and ADP of 124 he is great value, a 40 to 50 spot gap. At his Yahoo price around pick 70 he is riskier, but he beats that per game if he plays 60 games.
Even if he misses some time, his downside is low. He might play more minutes in his third season.
In an auction mock, Josh would pay up to 11 USD for him. He went for 20 USD, more than Franz Wagner or Jaren Jackson.
Memphis has a 4-4-4 schedule in weeks 19 to 21 with a March 28 end. It has only 13 back-to-backs, possibly the fewest in the league.
Memphis plays at a very high pace.

durable.text: He had foot surgery, then a second surgery after returning for 11 games. He has had three significant ankle or foot problems in his first two seasons.
The repeated ankle injury is a real concern. He is moving toward Kawhi and Embiid territory for health risk but is not there yet.
He was very healthy in college and played heavy minutes at Purdue without problems. His conditioning is good.
His FG% is elite on real volume. It clearly lifts a team's FG%.
His rebounds and blocks are far above the player pool.
He is a very good free throw shooter for a big, so he does not hurt FT% like most centers.
He is poor in assists, threes and steals, and makes almost no threes.
He commits many turnovers for a center.
He can handle high usage. On the court he was one of the most efficient and dominant players in the NBA, in a small sample.

note: Edey is a rare FG%, REB and BLK anchor at center. His weak spots are turnovers and threes, so he fits punt TO builds. The market splits on him: Yahoo values him at 16 USD with an average cost of 6.3 USD, ESPN at 2 USD, and he went for 2 USD in our league last season. In a mock he went for 20 USD while Josh capped him at 11 USD, so somewhere near 11 USD fairly prices his upside against his foot and ankle risk. Early in the season, check whether he gets more than the projected 25 to 28 minutes and how often Memphis rests him.
